source_text:
Ἅφρονες καὶ ἀσύνετοι καὶ μωροὶ καὶ ἀπαίδευτοι χλευάζουσιν ἡμᾶς καὶ μυκτηρίζουσιν, ἑαυτοὺς βουλόμενοι ἐπαίρεσθαι ταῖς διανοίαις αὐτῶν.
τί γὰρ δύναται θνητός; ἢ τίς ἰσχὺς γηγενοῦς;
γέγραπται γάρ: Οὐκ ἦν μορφὴ πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν μου, ἀλλ’ ἢ αὔραν καὶ φωνὴν ἤκουον:
Τί γάρ; μὴ καθαρὸς ἔσται βροτὸς ἔναντι κυρίου; ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων αὐτοῦ ἄμεμπτος ἀνήρ, εἰ κατὰ παίδων αὐτοῦ οὐ πιστεύει, κατὰ δὲ ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ σκολιόν τι ἐπενόησεν;
οὐρανὸς δὲ οὐ καθαρὸς ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ: ἔα δέ, οἱ κατοικοῦντες οἰκίας πηλίνας, ἐξ ὧν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐκ τοῦ αὐτοῦ πηλοῦ ἐσμεν: ἔπαισεν αὐτοὺς σητὸς τρόπον, καὶ ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν ἕως ἑσπέρας οὐκ ἔτι εἰσίν: παρὰ τὸ μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς ἑαυτοῖς βοηθῆσαι ἀπώλοντο.
ἐνεφύσησεν αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐτελεύτησαν παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν αὐτοὺς σοφίαν.
ἐπικάλεσαι δέ, εἴ τίς σοι ὑπακούσεται, ἤ εἴ τινα ἁγίων ἀγγέλων ὄψῃ: καὶ γὰρ ἄφρονα ἀναιρεῖ ὀργή. πεπλανημένον δὲ θανατοῖ ζῆλος.
ἐγὼ δὲ ἑώρακα ἄφρονας ῥίζας βάλλοντας, ἀλλ’ εὐθέως ἐβρώθη αὐτῶν ἡ δίαιτα.
πόρρω γένοιντο οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ σωτηρίας: κολαβρισθείησαν ἐπὶ θύραις ἡσσόνων, καὶ οὐκ ἔσται ὁ ἐξαιρούμενος: ἃ γὰρ ἐκείνοις ἡτοίμασται, δίκαιοι ἔδονται, αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐκ κακῶν οὐκ ἐξαίρετοι ἔσονται.
thought_title: Fools mock, but mortals are nothing before God
orientation: Clement has just urged humility and thanksgiving to God; now he quotes Scripture to show that foolish, untaught people mock the faithful, while no mortal is clean or strong before God.
pass_a_gloss: Fools and senseless and stupid and untaught [people] mock us and sneer [at us], wishing themselves to be lifted up in their minds. For what can a mortal [do]? Or what strength [has] an earth-born [one]? For it is written: There was no form before my eyes, but only a breeze and a voice I heard: What then? Shall a mortal be clean before the Lord? Or from his works [shall] a man [be] blameless, if against his children he does not trust, and against his angels he devised something crooked? And heaven [is] not clean before him: let alone, then, those dwelling in houses of clay, from which [clay] we ourselves also are from the same clay: he struck them in the manner of a moth, and from morning until evening they are no longer: because they could not help themselves they perished. He breathed into them, and they died because they did not have wisdom. But call, if anyone will answer you, or if you will see any of the holy angels: for anger destroys a fool, and envy kills the one led astray. But I have seen fools casting roots, but immediately their dwelling was devoured. Far may their sons be from salvation: may they be buffeted at doors of lesser [men], and there will be no one rescuing [them]: for what has been prepared for those, the righteous will eat, but they themselves will not be rescued from evils.

lemmas.gloss: sneer at, turn up the nose at

choices.term: ἄφρονες καὶ ἀσύνετοι καὶ μωροὶ καὶ ἀπαίδευτοι
choices.why: Four distinct adjectives pile up to describe the mockers; keeping all four preserves the rhetorical weight and each word's distinct shade.
rejected: fools and the senseless and the stupid and the untaught
foolish and senseless and stupid and uneducated

choices.term: ἑαυτοὺς βουλόμενοι ἐπαίρεσθαι ταῖς διανοίαις αὐτῶν
choices.english: wanting to exalt themselves in their own minds
choices.why: The reflexive with 'in their minds' shows the self-deception: their exaltation is internal, not real.
rejected: wishing to be lifted up in their thoughts
desiring to raise themselves in their own thinking

choices.why: The adjective echoes the creation theme from the previous section; 'clay' keeps the material, creaturely image.

choices.english: he struck them in the manner of a moth
choices.why: The moth image is vivid and sudden; 'struck' preserves the violence of the verb, and 'in the manner of' keeps the simile explicit.
rejected: he crushed them like a moth
he smote them as a moth

choices.why: The optative is a wish or curse; 'buffeted' captures the physical maltreatment implied by the rare verb.
The comparative 'lesser' is deliberately humiliating: they will be abused at the doors of those beneath them.

pass_b_english: Foolish, senseless, stupid, untaught people mock us and sneer at us, wanting to exalt themselves in their own minds.
For what can a mortal do? Or what strength does an earth-born person have?
For it is written: “There was no form before my eyes, but I heard a breeze and a voice:
What then? Will a mortal be pure before the Lord? Or will a man be blameless in his works, if God does not trust His own servants and perceives something crooked even in His angels?

Heaven itself is not pure in His sight. How much less those who live in houses of clay, since we ourselves are made from that same clay! He struck them as a moth does, and from morning until evening they are no more. Because they could not help themselves, they perished.
He breathed on them, and they died, because they had no wisdom.
But call out, if anyone will answer you, or if you will see any of the holy angels. For anger destroys the fool, and envy kills the one who has gone astray.
I have seen fools putting down roots, but immediately their way of life was devoured.

May their sons be far from salvation. May they be crushed at the doors of their inferiors, and may there be no one to rescue them. For what has been prepared for them, the righteous will eat, but they themselves will not be rescued from evils.”

problems.source_quote: εἰ κατὰ παίδων αὐτοῦ οὐ πιστεύει
problems.ruling: παίδων means 'children/servants'; in Job context 'servants' is standard, so not a major error.

problems.quote: buffeted at the doors of lesser men
problems.fix: bound at the doors of lesser men
problems.ruling: κολαβρισθείησαν relates to binding/handcuffing, not 'buffeted'; meaning changed.

problems.source_quote: Entire passage quoted in Greek does not correspond to Job 4:16‑5:5
problems.why: Citation does not match the quoted material
problems.fix: Remove or correct the citation to the appropriate source
problems.ruling: Passage spans Job 4:18–5:5, not 4:16–5:5; citation is wrong.

edits.old: buffeted at the doors of lesser men
edits.new: bound at the doors of lesser men

problems.quote: Will a mortal be pure before the Lord?
problems.source_quote: μὴ καθαρὸς ἔσται βροτὸς ἔναντι κυρίου
problems.why: Greek says ‘not pure’; English omits the negation, reversing the meaning.
problems.fix: Will a mortal be impure before the Lord?
problems.ruling: Greek μὴ καθαρὸς ἔσται means 'will NOT a mortal be pure'; English omits μὴ, reversing the rhetorical question's meaning.

edits.old: Will a mortal be pure before the Lord?
edits.new: Will a mortal be impure before the Lord?

fixed: The other previously tried edits were not confirmed problems in this round; only the negation issue required correction.

problems.quote: and perceives something crooked in his angels
problems.source_quote: κατὰ δὲ ἀγγέλων αὐτοῦ σκολιόν τι ἐπενόησεν
problems.why: κατά + genitive means 'concerning', not 'in'; it means 'and perceives something crooked concerning his angels'.
problems.fix: and perceives something crooked concerning his angels

problems.quote: but then, those who live in houses of clay
problems.source_quote: ἔα δέ, οἱ κατοικοῦντες οἰκίας πηλίνας
problems.why: ἔα δέ is an interjection 'behold!' or 'lo!', not 'but then'; it marks dramatic emphasis.
problems.fix: behold, those who dwell in houses of clay
problems.ruling: ἔα is an interjection ‘behold’, not ‘but then’; mis‑renders emphasis

problems.quote: may they be bound at the doors of lesser men
problems.why: κολαβρίζω means 'crushed/humbled', not 'bound'; 'may they be crushed at the doors of the inferior'.
problems.fix: may they be crushed at the doors of the inferior

edits.old: and perceives something crooked in his angels
edits.new: and perceives something crooked concerning his angels

edits.old: but then, those who live in houses of clay
edits.new: behold, those who dwell in houses of clay

edits.old: may they be bound at the doors of lesser men
edits.new: may they be crushed at the doors of the inferior

problems.quote: He crushes them as a moth is crushed
problems.why: Active aorist: he struck them moth-fashion. The English makes the moth the thing crushed.
problems.fix: He struck them as a moth does, and from morning until evening they are no more.
problems.ruling: ἔπαισεν is active aorist ('he struck them'), σητὸς τρόπον 'like a moth'; the English passive 'as a moth is crushed' makes the moth the victim, reversing the comparison.

problems.quote: May they be crushed at the doors of their inferiors
problems.why: κολαβρίζω means to be mocked or scoffed at. 'Crushed' gives the wrong sense and repeats the verb used for ἔπαισεν.
problems.fix: May they be mocked at the doors of their inferiors, and may there be no one to rescue them.
problems.ruling: κολαβρισθείησαν means be mocked or maltreated; “crushed” follows Hebrew דכא and repeats ἔπαισεν’s sense.

edits.old: He crushes them as a moth is crushed
edits.new: He struck them as a moth does

fixed: Fixed moth-clause: source ἔπαισεν αὐτοὺς σητὸς τρόπον is active he-struck them moth-fashion, so moth is not the thing crushed.
No edit for crushed at doors: source κολαβρισθείησαν ἐπὶ θύραις ἡσσόνων matches gloss buffeted and crushed in the gate, not mocked.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and referents in the long scriptural quotation, broke it into natural paragraphs, removed the em dash, and made the divine subject explicit where the source implies God.

last_rejected.quote: but immediately their way of life was devoured
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ’ εὐθέως ἐβρώθη αὐτῶν ἡ δίαιτα
last_rejected.why: δίαιτα here means dwelling/habitation, not 'way of life'; Job 4:21 LXX context is their tent being consumed.
last_rejected.fix: but immediately their dwelling was devoured
last_rejected.ruling: δίαιτα = diet, livelihood; 'way of life' is a permissible rendering, not a substantive meaning shift

last_rejected.quote: but I heard a breeze and a voice
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀλλ’ ἢ αὔραν καὶ φωνὴν ἤκουον
last_rejected.why: αὔραν means “sound” or “noise”, not “breeze”. The English adds a false element.
last_rejected.fix: but I heard a sound and a voice
last_rejected.ruling: αὔρα can mean 'breeze' or 'whisper'; 'breeze' is within normal range, not a mistranslation.
